title: Democrats Shouldn’t Squander Their Chance to Launch a Foreign Policy Revolution
gist: Matthew Duss argues the incoming Democratic congressional majority (taking control in January after the November 2026 midterms) should immediately use the power of the purse, including threatening a shutdown at the December 11 continuing-resolution deadline, to end Trump's Iran war, while tying foreign policy to an aggressive anticorruption and cost-of-living agenda. He frames Trump's unilateral warmaking as an aggressive expression of a bipartisan militarist mindset rather than a break from it.

themes.theme: Ending the Iran war via the power of the purse

insights.claim: The author argues the new Democratic-controlled Congress's first and most urgent task should be ending the U.S. war with Iran, a conflict that has grown less popular as Americans feel its effects on their wallets.
insights.speaker: Matthew Duss
insights.so_what: A Democratic Congress pushing to defund the Iran war raises the odds of de-escalation, relevant to oil risk premia and defense names.
insights.quote: The first and most urgent task will be ending the Iran war, a reckless and unpopular conflict that has become even less popular as Americans have felt its effects on their wallets.

insights.claim: Democrats should be prepared to block the National Defense Authorization Act and oppose all Pentagon funding to force an end to hostilities in Iran.

insights.claim: The author urges Democrats to threaten another government shutdown at the December 11 continuing-resolution deadline unless the funding bill prohibits any money for the Iran war.

insights.claim: The author argues Democrats' foreign policy should be tied to cost of living, confronting reckless tariffs while accepting that the neoliberal taboo on tariffs is a thing of the past.
